summary: Markets face severe disruption centered on Nvidia amid executive turmoil, regulatory crackdowns on China chip exports, and rising political pressure on AI data center expansion and energy costs.

picks.name: Unusual Whales
picks.text: JUST IN: Nvidia’s $NVDA board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang, its founder and chief executive, per the WSJ
picks.why: Board preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang creates severe leadership and governance crisis for a bellwether stock.

picks.name: Unusual Whales
picks.text:
BREAKING: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick repeatedly held up restrictions on Nvidia $NVDA chip exports to China, even after Trump approved them three times, per Axios.

At an Oval Office meeting, Trump asked Elon Musk for his view; Musk backed tighter controls, along with Rubio, Bessent and Hegseth. Lutnick warned the move “will start a trade war with China.” Trump ordered: “Let’s get it done.”

The restrictions still haven’t been put in place,
picks.why: White House pushes through tighter chip export controls to China despite commerce secretary pushback, impacting semiconductor supply chains.

picks.name: Unusual Whales
picks.text:
Microsoft , $MSFT, says it will “pay our own way” to power its data centers, without government subsidies or pushing up electricity costs for other customers, per Bloomberg.

“We don’t want other customers to be paying for our growth,” said Noelle Walsh, president of Microsoft’s cloud operations.

Microsoft is spending about $117 billion this year on AI and cloud data centers, and says it will keep building.
picks.why: Microsoft commits to funding its own data center power infrastructure to avoid grid strain, highlighting massive capex and utility costs.

picks.name: Unusual Whales
picks.text:
BREAKING: Senator Josh Hawley has endorsed a temporary pause on data center construction, becoming the highest-ranking Republican to back a nationwide moratorium.

“Senator Hawley is calling for a federal data center moratorium until Congress passes a bill of rights giving taxpayers guarantees of no rate increases,” a Hawley spokesperson said.
picks.why: Legislative push for a federal data center moratorium threatens near-term infrastructure buildouts and power demand growth.

picks.name: Unusual Whales
picks.text:
Sam Altman told Samsung executives that AI demand has been “double counted,” according to Korea’s Financial News.

In a closed-door session with about 50 Samsung presidents on Oct 31, Altman reportedly said only OpenAI and Anthropic are driving major demand growth. 

He warned of supply shocks and turbulence ahead but said he expects AI demand to surge in the long run.
picks.why: OpenAI leadership warns of 'double counted' AI demand and potential supply shocks ahead, creating growth doubts for hardware suppliers.

picks.name: Unusual Whales
picks.text:
Anthropic is expected to go public next week, at $70 to $78 per share.

There is a 46% chance that the valuation hits $1.5 trillion to $1.75 trillion, per Polymarket⁠.com. https://t.co/RaWUfXJvfv
picks.why: Anthropic IPO expected next week with high targeted valuation, serving as a major liquidity test for the generative AI sector.
